policy: Distillation training data in this programme comes from exactly two kinds of source: (1) prompts with an open licence, whose responses are REGENERATED by our own open teacher — never the dataset's bundled responses; (2) data we wrote ourselves. Anything whose response side was produced by a closed model is refused, however good it is. This mirrors the grok kit rule: open weights as teachers, never xAI or any closed model's outputs.

sources.use: prompts only — the first user turn of each conversation. Bundled assistant responses are DISCARDED by prepare_distill_data.py; every response in the training set is generated by our teacher (see teacher_generate.py).

sources.role: on-distribution prompt source — the programme's own seed prompts
sources.use: prompts as-is; responses generated by our teacher. Cross-reference: show/production/wielder/grok-local/training/ (sibling lane's file; this kit reads it at job time, never vendors a copy).

sources.role: task-specific prompts written for the show/game programme
sources.use: drop .jsonl files of {"prompt": ...} beside the manifest; they join the prompt pool with provenance recorded.

sources.licence: ODC-By 1.0 for the collection, mixed per-subset
sources.use: REFUSED as a whole: the mixture contains non-commercial subsets (e.g. No Robots, CC-BY-NC-4.0) and subsets whose responses were generated by GPT-4 (e.g. WildChat GPT-4) — closed-model outputs, barred by policy. A future filtered variant may use ONLY named clean subsets (open-licence prompts, responses regenerated by our teacher), with the subset list recorded here before use.

sources.licence: per-card: dataset is a compilation; provenance of many subsets traces to GPT-4 generations
sources.use: REFUSED: much of the response side is closed-model output. Same rule as Tulu.

sources.id: any dataset of xAI / OpenAI / Anthropic model outputs
sources.use: REFUSED, permanently, by the owner's open-teacher-only rule. Teachers in this kit are open-weight models we serve ourselves.
